works.version: Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research A 503, 496–503 (2003), publisher version, DOI 10.1016/S0168-9002(03)01005-2
scope: PDF1–2 fragment separation and optical layout
PDF3–4 magnet parameters, transfer matrix and operations
PDF5–6 commissioning, TOF and energy-loss identification, F4 profiles
PDF7–8 beam species examples, conclusion context and references
checks: First-page imprint and DOI confirm the original; ignore conflicting DOI in the reading return.
PDF5 Fig. 4 and text: A/ΔA>300 inferred from the 16O TOF projection, and silicon thickness 300 µm checked visually.
PDF5–6 Fig. 5: 47% is the 17F fraction with the stated degrader in the 80 MeV/u 20Ne commissioning configuration, not an efficiency for arbitrary beams.
PDF6 Sec. 3 reports F4 beam widths; Fig. 6 instead shows light neutron-rich nuclides from the 18O example.
works.gap: The design values and commissioning observations have their own conditions. RIBLL1 parameters do not identify the RIBLL2 settings of the later 16C experiment.
works.lineage: Original early RIBLL instrument and commissioning article. The HIRFL-CSR RIBLL2 experiment is a separate installation lineage.
